title: The section of the comparison square and the open it fixes
statement:
Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be
proper and let
$j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ be
open immersions with
$u j_1=j_2$. For $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$, with projections
$b:V\to T_1$, $p:V\to X$ and the morphism $s:X\to V$ induced by
$j_1$ of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], the morphism
$s$ is an
open immersion with
$p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_X$ whose image is open and closed in
$V$, and $s$ identifies $X$ with the open subscheme $j_1(X)$
of $V$, the projection $b$ identifying $V$ with the open
subscheme $u^{-1}(j_2(X))$ of $T_1$.

proof.text: The pair $(j_1,\operatorname{id}_X)$ satisfies $u\circ j_1=j_2\circ\operatorname{id}_X$. The fibre-product universal property gives the unique $s:X\to V$ with $b\circ s=j_1$ and $p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_X$. These are precisely the defining equations for the section named in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]; this argument uses only its geometric data, and no sheaf or coefficient hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, construction of s from the pair (j_1,id_X)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] to $j_2:X\hookrightarrow T_2$ and $u:T_1\to T_2$. It gives an open immersion $c:X\times_{T_2}T_1\to T_1$. The universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] gives a map $\tau:V\to X\times_{T_2}T_1$ with components $(p,b)$ and a reverse map with the reversed projections. Each composite has the same two projections as the identity, so uniqueness makes them inverse. Thus $b=c\circ\tau$ is an open immersion: composing the open-subscheme isomorphism for $c$ with the isomorphism $\tau$ preserves that identification, by [def-weil-open-immersion].

Put $O=j_2(X)$ and $U=u^{-1}(O)\subseteq T_1$. The cartesian equation $u b=j_2 p$ gives $b(V)\subseteq U$. Conversely, on the open subscheme $(U,\mathcal O_{T_1}|_U)$, restrict the underlying map and structure-sheaf map of $u$ to the open $O$, and then compose with the inverse of the open-subscheme isomorphism $j_2:X\xrightarrow{\sim}(O,\mathcal O_{T_2}|_O)$. This gives a morphism $q:U\to X$ with $j_2q=u|_U$. The pair $(U\hookrightarrow T_1,q)$ therefore gives a morphism $U\to V$ by the fibre-product universal property. Its composite with $b$ is the inclusion of $U$, proving $U\subseteq b(V)$. Consequently $b(V)=U$, and the open-immersion definition identifies $V$ with $(U,\mathcal O_{T_1}|_U)$.

source.place: Proof, identification of the image of b (elementary open-subscheme restriction argument)

proof.text: Under this identification of $V$ with $U$, the equality $b s=j_1$ says that the underlying map of $s$ is the homeomorphism of $X$ onto $j_1(X)\subseteq U$. This is open in $U$, since $j_1(X)$ is open in $T_1$. Both $b$ and $j_1$ identify the relevant structure sheaves with restrictions of $\mathcal O_{T_1}$; the composite sheaf map for $b s=j_1$ forces the sheaf map for $s$ to be the corresponding restriction isomorphism (cancel the isomorphism supplied by $b$). Hence $s$ is an open immersion and identifies $X$ with the open subscheme $j_1(X)$ of $V$.

source.place: Proof, s is the restriction of j_1 to the open subscheme b(V)

proof.text: [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-p-proper] applies to the given proper $u$ and open immersion $j_2$, and states that this projection $p:V\to X$ is proper and separated. We have proved that $s$ is an open immersion, and step 1 supplies $p s=\operatorname{id}_X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-section-clopen] with $S=X$ to obtain that $s(X)$ is open and closed in $V$, including the decomposition into the two complementary open subschemes. This proves all the clauses of the statement.

lean.statement: theorem properOpenSectionProperties {T₁ T₂ X : Scheme.{u}} (u : T₁ ⟶ T₂) [IsProper u] (j₁ : X ⟶ T₁) (j₂ : X ⟶ T₂) [IsOpenImmersion j₁] [IsOpenImmersion j₂] (h : j₁ ≫ u = j₂) : IsOpenImmersion (properOpenSection u j₁ j₂ h) ∧ properOpenSection u j₁ j₂ h ≫ (pullback.snd u j₂) = 𝟙 X ∧ IsClopen (Set.range (properOpenSection u j₁ j₂ h).base) ∧ Set.range (properOpenSection u j₁ j₂ h).base = (pullback.fst u j₂).base ⁻¹' Set.range j₁.base ∧ IsOpenImmersion (pullback.fst u j₂) ∧ Set.range (pullback.fst u j₂) = (u.base ⁻¹' Set.range j₂.base)
